Now speaking

Morning, George — it's Saturday the fifteenth, and it's shaping up to be a scorcher.

Athens is pushing the mid-thirties with the Meltemi roaring back in, so the whole country's on a very-high fire alert today; if you're heading for rock, pick your spot with that in mind.

— personal items —

Let's go overseas first.

Japan's Chiba region, just east of Tokyo, got hammered by the heaviest rain in its record books — over three hundred and fifty millimetres in a single day, the first ever top-level emergency warning there, and at least eight people killed as roads turned to rivers and hillsides gave way.

Thousands spent the night in shelters, and one person's still missing.

And today marks five years since the Taliban swept back into Kabul.

Half a decade on, the U.N. calls it the world's harshest regime for women and girls — around two and a half million girls still shut out of secondary school, and close to a hundred edicts stripping away work, movement, even the right to be heard in public.

A grim anniversary worth a moment.

Your science note's a good one for a climber.

A huge University of East Anglia review, nearly half a million people tracked for fourteen years, found that people who regularly take the stairs had a twenty-four percent lower chance of dying from any cause, and thirty-nine percent lower from heart disease.

The sweet spot was about six flights a day.

So skip the lift — your legs already agree.

On the tech beat, the big Western labs were quiet, but China's Z-A-I dropped GLM five-point-three, and it's now the strongest open coding model anyone's measured, edging past the paid frontier on some benchmarks.

Two catches worth knowing as a founder: the weights aren't actually public yet — they're promised in about two weeks, after safety checks — and the same training push gave it a surprisingly sharp knack for finding software exploits, which is either a gift or a headache depending which side of the fence you're on.

Closer to home, the fire service has all of Attica and four other regions on a category-four, very-high risk today as the Meltemi picks up; up north this week a wall of flames even pushed beachgoers into the sea.

Steer well clear of the pine hills.

World

  • Record rain floods Japan’s Chiba region. The heaviest daily rainfall in the local record — over 350 mm in a single day — triggered flooding and landslides just east of Tokyo, killing at least 8 people, with one still missing. Japan issued its highest-level emergency warning there for the first time; thousands sheltered overnight. The Watchers
  • Five years of Taliban rule in Afghanistan. Today marks half a decade since the Taliban retook Kabul. The UN calls it the world’s harshest regime for women and girls — roughly 2.4 million girls still shut out of secondary school, and close to 100 edicts restricting work, movement and public life. Al Jazeera
  • Science: take the stairs, live longer. A University of East Anglia meta-analysis of nearly 480,000 people tracked for ~14 years found regular stair-climbers had a 24% lower risk of death from any cause and 39% lower from heart disease — sweet spot around six flights a day. ScienceDaily
